reason: Both conversations correctly issue the critical safety stop ('stop using, don't keep resetting, don't open it, engineer'), so neither fails on safety. Conversation 1 stops there with a generic one-liner that never even mentions the microwave, offers no explanation to a homeowner who doesn't know what an RCD is, and asks nothing. Conversation 2 gives the same stop plus a plain-language reason, correctly names a door interlock/earth-leakage fault as a candidate, explicitly warns off opening the case because of the high-voltage parts, asks one efficient question that surfaced the extension lead and the internal bang, and escalates appropriately without recommending any part. Its weaknesses are leaning on 'most likely magnetron/capacitor' speculation, loosely calling an RCD trip an 'overload', and not suggesting the check of whether the RCD stays set with the microwave unplugged, but it still serves the homeowner clearly better than Conversation 1's bare boilerplate.
